_doc: Scene catalog: the only scene types a storyboard may use. A storyboard picks types and fills params; the engine (studio/engine/) draws them in the channel's look. status 'built' = implemented and seen on real contact sheets; 'built-untested' = implemented, not yet used by an episode. Event verbs the engine knows: reveal, draw, count_start, count_stop, highlight, verdict, emphasize; any other verb is drawn as 'emphasize' and listed in build/engine_report.json. Props: see 'props'. Adding a type or prop is an engine change.

title_card.purpose: Big hook text with one supporting prop. The first 1-2 s of most Shorts.

params.prop: optional prop from 'props'; prop_args optional (e.g. {"colors": [...]} for a real flag)

map_focus.purpose: Real Natural Earth map; zoom to a region, highlight it, drop pins.

params.region: [west, south, east, north] in degrees, or an ISO alpha-2 code
params.detail: optional list of {osm: '<place name>', iso: 'BE'}: draws that place's OpenStreetMap boundary (enclaves, villages) on top, credited on screen

map_route.purpose: Animated path or arrows across a real map (routes, invasions, migrations).

params.label: string
params.highlight: optional; inherited from neighbouring map scenes on the same region

count_up.purpose: A number that counts to its value, with a unit and an optional qualifier ('the major's own count').

params.qualifier: optional string, required when the claim is an estimate

versus.purpose: Two things side by side with a verdict (organ vs organ, army vs emus). With {code, name} objects on both sides it draws the ranked channel's Broadcast 'tale of the tape' card (waving flags, metric rows) for the Country vs country series.

params.left: subject (prop id or text), or {code, name} for a country card
params.country card only: title, source (required, on screen), rows [{label, left, right, decimals?}] (real numbers), verdict_side left|right (default centre). Events: reveal (one per row, in order), verdict

ranking_bars.purpose: Static ranked bars from a dataset (ranked channel, 'Flag Badges' look): round flag badges with faces ride the bar tips, medal rank circles, confetti and a crown on #1, and the highlighted country (worried, or parked below the chart and shocked when it is outside the top N). The source line is on screen the whole scene.

params.dataset: path to a data file inside the episode (JSON or CSV, see studio/engine/scenes/ranking.js header): rows of code (ISO alpha-2), name, value, plus a source string (required, drawn on screen), metric, decimals, prefix, suffix
params.highlight: optional ISO code. Inside the top N: its bar turns red and the leader gets gold. Outside: it is parked below the chart with its true rank
params.title: optional string, <= 2 lines (defaults to the dataset title)

ranking_bars.events: reveal {rank?}: reveals rank N, N-1 ... 1 in order on the spoken word (or the named rank); highlight: the underdog beat (defaults to just after the crown); emphasize {code?}: pulses a badge. Flags come from studio/engine/flags.js; a code with no drawing gets a neutral badge and an engine warning.

ranking_race.purpose: Bar-chart race through years from a dataset: bars re-rank smoothly (overtakes glide), values interpolate between real data years (the source line says so), a big year counter, crown follows the leader, the highlighted country worries and is parked when it drops out of the top N.

params.dataset: path in the episode; JSON rows {code, name, values: {year: number}} or CSV long format code,name,year,value; plus source (required)
params.title: optional string

ranking_race.events: any event with args.year pins that year to the spoken word (linear between pins; repeat a year to hold it); highlight: activates the highlighted country; emphasize {code}: pulses that badge.

character_dialog.purpose: Two or more cast members talking; each spoken para with a speaker animates that character.

params.setting: set id: bloodstream, neurons, stomach, gut or spotlight
params.title: optional big title on the stage until the first bubble (spotlight opener)
params.bubbles: optional {paragraph id: bubble text}; default is the paragraph's caption text

character_explain.purpose: One cast member presents a diagram or prop.

params.speaker: cast id
params.setting: set id: bloodstream, neurons, stomach, gut or spotlight
params.steps: optional list of {label, at} chips that pop in on their cues

stamp_reveal.purpose: Rubber-stamp punchline word slammed over the previous scene, which keeps playing underneath.

params.dy: optional px offset down from stage centre, to keep the stamp off the text underneath

quote_card.purpose: A sourced quotation, typeset, with speaker and year. The voice reads it. The text is on screen for the whole time it is being read.

timeline.purpose: Horizontal timeline with dated events popping in.

diagram_callout.purpose: A drawn object with labelled callouts (a gun, a cell, a reactor).

split_compare.purpose: Before and after, or expectation and reality, in two panels.

custom.purpose: Escape hatch: a one-off scene written in code. Needs a stronger model or a human review; use sparingly (target: under 20% of runtime).

params.fn: name of a function in the episode's scenes.js
params.why: one sentence on why no catalog type fits

outro_loop.purpose: Final beat that visually matches the first frame, so the Short loops cleanly.

params.echo_of: scene id of the opening scene

map_history.purpose: Borders morph or recolour between dated snapshots of a territory, with a big year counter; geometry from OpenHistoricalMap (CC0 unless a relation's license tag says otherwise) or merged Natural Earth units (approximate). The engine draws the credit 'Historical borders: OpenHistoricalMap contributors'. Run studio/tools/geo.py to fetch and cache geometry; licence tags land in build/geo.json (ohm_licenses, ohm_non_cc0).

params.focus: [west, south, east, north] or an ISO alpha-2 code
params.snapshots: list of {date: 'YYYY[-MM[-DD]]' (the dataset's date, shown on screen), at: cue where this snapshot replaces the previous one (omit on the first), approximate: optional bool, territories: [{key, name, color, and ONE of relation: <OHM relation id> | ohm_name: '<OHM admin_level 2 name; resolved to the relation valid on date>' | iso: ['MX', ...] (Natural Earth units merged; forces the 'approximate' label)}]}. Territories with the same key morph between snapshots.
